subject: GCP Marketplace: invoice shows overlapping daily windows causing duplicated usage lines
messages:
From: Marcus Ellis <marcus.ellis@acmecloud.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: billing@acmecloud.com
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discrepancy on Apr billing — duplicated daily lines for several SKUs

Hi Neha,

We're seeing duplicated daily usage lines on the Apr GCP Marketplace invoice for our Acme account (customer id 5547). Example: the same SKU (redwood-inference.tokens.standard) appears twice for 2027-04-24 in separate lines with nearly identical quantities and charges. That caused an overcharge of ~USD 1,900 on our April invoice.

I attached a CSV (acme_gcp_invoice_202704.csv) with the invoice export and a short metering export we pulled from our side. We suspect this is related to the way daily windows were computed around 00:00 UTC -> 01:00 local transition for several projects; the totals match if you collapse overlapping windows, but the marketplace invoice did not.

We need:
- A quick confirmation whether this is a Redwood billing-side issue or GCP aggregation behavior.
- If it's Redwood-side, a proposed credit memo and ETA for reversal.
- VAT implications: invoice already published and tax entries posted on our side — will need a corrected VAT invoice.

Short timeline please — our AP team has put the payment on hold pending reconciliation.

Thanks,
Marcus
Senior Finance Ops, Acme Cloud Solutions
Acme Cloud | partner-ops@acmecloud.com

Attachments: acme_gcp_invoice_202704.csv (CSV, 42KB), metering-export-20270424.json (JSON, 150KB), screenshot-invoice-lines.png (PNG, 120KB)
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Ellis <marcus.ellis@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Discrepancy on Apr billing — duplicated daily lines for several SKUs

Marcus — thanks for the clear examples and attachments. We're looking into this as high priority. Quick notes:

- Initial hypothesis: an overlap between Redwood's usage-window aggregation (we bucket by customer-local day to support entity attribution) and GCP's marketplace metering timestamps during a DST-like shift can produce duplicated line items if two ingestion batches both materialize the same window.
- Karthik (copied) will pull the raw per-request metering logs and our aggregation traces for the affected account and date window.
- Marissa will coordinate accounting and VAT impacts if a credit memo is needed.

Deliverables by EOD tomorrow (26 Apr):
1) Reconciled usage CSV that collapses duplicates with reasoning column.
2) Root cause summary (ingestion order, batching window, any late-arriving records).
3) Draft credit memo amount and VAT correction language for your AP.

Can you confirm the exact customer entity (taxable entity id) you used to book the invoice? That will help Marissa scope the VAT correction.

I'll keep you posted.

—Neha
Sr. Revenue Ops, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marcus Ellis <marcus.ellis@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 11:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Discrepancy on Apr billing — duplicated daily lines for several SKUs

Marcus, Neha — I pulled the ingestion traces and the marketplace batching logs for Acme (customer id 5547). Findings so far:

- On 2027-04-24 between 23:45 UTC and 01:15 UTC (account local timezone UTC-1 for the projects in question), we see two ingestion batches that both contained a set of usage events for project: acme-prod-5547. Both batches were processed by our aggregator because late-arriving events triggered a re-materialization of the same daily bucket.
- Our reconciliation step is supposed to idempotently merge late events into the existing bucket; in this case, an edge-case race condition allowed duplicate lines to persist in the marketplace CSV export.
- There is no indication that GCP sent duplicate meterings; the raw metering-export-20270424.json (attached) matches exactly one set of events. The duplication happened during our bucket flattening step prior to generating the invoice file for marketplace listing.

Action plan:
A) Generate reconciled invoice lines (collapse duplicate lines, keep original timestamps for audit) — ETA: 12 hours.
B) Produce internal postmortem describing the race condition and a patch to the bucket materializer to dedupe on (customer, sku, window-start, usage-id) — ETA: patch + test 10 business days.
C) If Acme wants a credit memo, we'll propose a reversal now and then run an automated verification on the next billing cycle to ensure no residual duplicates.

Marissa — can you prepare the VAT reversal template once we have the reconciled amount? This will determine whether Acme needs a corrected tax invoice or a credit note (country-specific).

-Karthik
Engineering Lead, Inference Billing
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Ellis <marcus.ellis@acmecloud.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Discrepancy on Apr billing — duplicated daily lines for several SKUs

Marcus — thanks for flagging the tax question. Two quick notes from the finance side:

- We can issue a credit memo for the USD 1,900 once Karthik's reconciled CSV is finalized. For VAT: since the original invoice was already recorded, in most EU jurisdictions we'd issue a credit note referencing the original tax invoice number and either a corrected invoice (if requested) or a separate VAT credit note. For the US, VAT isn't applicable, but state-level tax reversals may be necessary depending on where the customer booked the tax.
- Please confirm Acme's taxable entity and VAT registration country (if applicable). Also confirm whether AP needs the credit memo to be sent to a specific billing contact or if the invoice contact (billing@acmecloud.com) is OK.

Next steps from Redwood finance:
1) We will prepare a draft credit memo (Proposed amount: USD 1,900) and a VAT credit note template (if required) and send both to you for acceptance.
2) If accepted, Redwood will create the marketplace credit memo and notify GCP (if marketplace process requires it) — timeline typically 5-7 business days after acceptance.
3) We'll include a short audit bundle (reconciled CSV + reconciliation notes) for your AP.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Revenue Accounting Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Ellis <marcus.ellis@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 02 May 2027 10:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Discrepancy on Apr billing — duplicated daily lines for several SKUs

Marcus — updating the thread with the reconciled deliverable. Attached: reconciled-acme-usage-20270424.csv (collapsed duplicates) and reconciliation-notes.txt (short explanation). Summary:

- Reconciled overcharge: USD 1,912.43 (pre-tax).
- Root cause: race in the bucket materializer allowing a late-arriving re-materialization of an already materialized daily bucket for projects in UTC-1 window.
- Remediation: fix queued for next sprint (will prevent duplicate materialization), and we'll add a post-export dedupe guard for the immediate release.

Marissa will follow up with the credit memo and VAT wording. Marcus — please confirm the billing contact and the tax entity so we can finalize the credit note. Once you accept the credit memo we'll issue it and provide the AP bundle so you can release the payment hold.

Thanks for the patience and apologies for the disruption.

—Neha

Attachments referenced in-thread: reconciled-acme-usage-20270424.csv (CSV, 12KB), reconciliation-notes.txt (TXT, 3KB)
